name: userdel
description: Deletes a user account and optionally its home directory and mail spool.

flags.description: Remove the home directory and mail spool along with the account.
Force removal even if the user is logged in.

examples.explanation: Removes the account bob but leaves /home/bob in place — the safe default.
Removes the account AND the home directory. Make sure the data is backed up first.
After deleting a user, locates files still owned by the old UID so you can reassign or remove them.

about: userdel removes entries from /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, and /etc/group. Files owned by the user elsewhere in the filesystem (e.g. in /tmp or /var/www) are NOT removed; searching by UID finds them.
useCases: Clean up departed users on shared servers.
mistakes: Deleting a user whose processes are still running — the processes keep running under an orphaned UID.
Assuming -r cleans everything; stray files owned by the UID remain elsewhere.
warnings: userdel -r irreversibly deletes the home directory. Back up or archive first.
